Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Depressive symptom scores (CES-D) did not differ between T2DM patients with vitamin D insufficiency and those with normal vitamin D.
Sentence: "There was no significant difference between groups with regard to the indices of blood lipid, liver function, and scores in CES-D and PSQI."
Measured as: CES-D score
Population: 132 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
Intervention: Vitamin D insufficiency (plasma 25(OH)D <29 ng/mL), measured not given
Comparator: Normal vitamin D (25(OH)D ≥29 ng/mL)
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 132
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Depressive symptoms (BDI-II) were lower in vitamin D-treated women than in untreated women with Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
Sentence: "The BDI-II score was lowest in the vitamin D-treated women and highest in the untreated patients with thyroiditis."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (BDI-II)
Population: Young euthyroid women with Hashimoto's thyroiditis, untreated or receiving vitamin D, selenomethionine or myo-inositol
Intervention: Vitamin D (dose and duration not reported)
Comparator: Untreated women, and women receiving selenomethionine or myo-inositol
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

  "rationale": "The studies enrolled distinct clinical populations (type 2 diabetes patients vs young women with Hashimoto's thyroiditis) and examined different exposures (endogenous vitamin D insufficiency vs exogenous vitamin D supplementation).",
